newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Adventists likely to have cast special votes.
newsitem.headline: NZ Adventists likely to have cast special votes.

text.p: New Zealand's 10,000 adult Seventh Day Adventists were likely to have cast special votes because their faith puts Saturday off limits, church spokesman Bill Townend said on Tuesday.
"It's each individual's call but generally there would have been a lot of Seventh Day Adventist people who would have cast a special vote," he told Reuters.
Townend said he had no indication as to which way members would have voted.
"No, not really. We have a pretty broad cross section of people and that would be reflected in their voting. We have a lot of Pacific Island people in Auckland particularly," he said.
After Saturday's election, the Christian Coalition polled 4.35 percent of the party vote, just short of the five percent needed to gain representation in Parliament.
The electoral office was not able to give an immediate answer on how many special votes would be needed for the Christian Coalition to reach the five percent threshold.
